era: Licensed monster truck racing and freestyle games
summary: Official Monster Jam games across Ubisoft, Activision, GameMill, THQ Nordic, Rainbow Studios, and Milestone, covering combat, arcade racing, freestyle, stadium events, and modern open-world Monster Jam formats.

entries.title: Monster Jam: Maximum Destruction

emulation.notes: Use the Windows version as primary.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: PC route exceeds original console/handheld fidelity

primary.why: Maximum Destruction released on Windows, PlayStation 2, GameCube, and Game Boy Advance. The Windows version is the highest-fidelity configurable route for the licensed vehicular-combat Monster Jam game.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows PC version; use PS2/GameCube as console alternatives and GBA only for portable preservation.

entries.remaster_caveats: No sourced remaster or complete edition.

entries.title: Monster 4x4: Masters of Metal

emulation.notes: Use PCSX2 for the primary route.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Sixth-generation console fidelity with emulator upscaling

primary.why: Masters of Metal is licensed by and loosely based on Monster Jam, with real Monster Jam trucks, and released on PlayStation 2 and GameCube. With no PC version sourced, PlayStation 2 is the primary preservation route.
primary.how_to_play: Play on original PlayStation 2 hardware or PCSX2; use GameCube as an alternate console route.

entries.remaster_caveats: No sourced remaster. Later Monster 4x4 games drop the Monster Jam license and should be treated as their own franchise.

entries.title: Monster Jam

emulation.emulator: Native Windows / PCSX2 / Dolphin / Xenia / melonDS
emulation.notes: Use the Windows version as primary.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: PC route exceeds original console/handheld fidelity

primary.why: Monster Jam released on Windows, PlayStation 2, Wii, Xbox 360, and Nintendo DS. The Windows version is the highest-fidelity configurable route for the Activision/Torus game with 20 real Monster Jam trucks, stadium drag racing, off-road racing, and freestyle.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows PC version; use Xbox 360/Wii/PS2 as console alternatives and DS only for portable preservation.

entries.remaster_caveats: No sourced remaster or complete edition.

entries.title: Monster Jam: Urban Assault

emulation.notes: Use Dolphin for the primary route.

primary.why: Urban Assault released on PlayStation 2, PSP, Nintendo DS, and Wii. With no PC or HD console release sourced, Wii is the strongest full-console route, while PSP and DS are portable access routes.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Wii version on original hardware or Dolphin; use PS2 as an alternate console route and PSP/DS only for portable preservation.

entries.remaster_caveats: No sourced remaster or PC release.

entries.title: Monster Jam: Path of Destruction

emulation.notes: Use Xenia or original Xbox 360 hardware for the primary route.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: HD console presentation with emulator upscaling

primary.why: Path of Destruction released on Wii, PlayStation 3, Xbox 360, Nintendo DS, and PSP. The Xbox 360 release is a high-fidelity HD route for the game with 28 licensed trucks, custom truck creation, and head-to-head multiplayer.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Xbox 360 release on original hardware or Xenia; use PS3 as the alternate HD route and handheld/Wii versions for preservation.

entries.remaster_caveats: No sourced remaster or complete edition.

entries.title: Monster Jam (iOS)

emulation.notes: Use compatible iOS hardware/account access if available.

primary.why: The 2014 Monster Jam iOS game is a distinct GameMill mobile release with 2.5D events and 24 licensed trucks. It predates the expanded Battlegrounds release and remains its own mobile-only route.
primary.how_to_play: Play on a compatible iOS device if the app is still owned/available; otherwise preserve as a historical mobile entry.

entries.remaster_caveats: Mobile app availability may be delisted or device-dependent.

entries.title: Monster Jam Battlegrounds

emulation.notes: Use the Windows version as primary.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: PC route exceeds original console fidelity

primary.why: Monster Jam Battlegrounds is an expanded, updated version of the 2014 iOS game released on Windows, PlayStation 3, and Xbox 360. Windows is the highest-fidelity configurable route for its 2.5D trials-style events, stadium races, and freestyle events.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows PC/Steam version; use PS3 or Xbox 360 only as console alternatives.

entries.remaster_caveats: The earlier iOS game has a different truck count and is preserved as its own entry.

entries.title: Monster Jam: Crush It!

emulation.notes: Use PS4 or Xbox One hardware; Switch is portable alternative.

primary.why: Crush It! released on PlayStation 4 and Xbox One in 2016, then Nintendo Switch in 2017. With no PC version sourced, PlayStation 4 is the primary home-console route and Switch is a portable alternative.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PlayStation 4 version; use Xbox One as an equivalent console alternative and Switch only for portable play.

entries.remaster_caveats: No sourced PC release, remaster, or complete edition.

entries.title: Monster Jam Steel Titans

emulation.notes: Run natively on Windows at the highest stable settings.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: PC route exceeds original console/portable/cloud fidelity

primary.why: Steel Titans released on Windows, PlayStation 4, Xbox One, Nintendo Switch, and later Google Stadia. Windows is the highest-fidelity configurable route for the Rainbow Studios game with an explorable off-road environment, career, stadium events, and over 30 trucks.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows PC version at the highest stable settings; use PS4/Xbox One as console alternatives and Switch only for portable play.

entries.remaster_caveats: Google Stadia is no longer a playable access route after the service shutdown.

entries.title: Monster Jam Steel Titans 2

emulation.notes: Run natively on Windows at the highest stable settings.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: PC route exceeds original console/portable/cloud fidelity

primary.why: Steel Titans 2 released on Windows, PlayStation 4, Xbox One, Nintendo Switch, and Google Stadia, with some listings also including PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S routes. Windows is the highest-fidelity configurable route for the expanded sequel.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows PC version at the highest stable settings; use modern console versions only as access alternatives.

entries.remaster_caveats: Google Stadia is no longer playable; PS5/Xbox Series X/S listings should be rechecked at storefront level if native-release precision is required.

entries.title: Monster Jam Showdown
entries.definitive_edition: Windows PC release with owned DLC

emulation.notes: Run natively on Windows at the highest stable settings with owned DLC installed.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: PC release at highest stable settings

primary.why: Monster Jam Showdown released on Windows, Nintendo Switch, PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Xbox One, and Xbox Series X/S. It uses Unreal Engine 5, includes 40 base licensed trucks and 26 DLC trucks, and supports split-screen and online multiplayer; Windows is the highest-fidelity configurable route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows PC version from Steam or Epic Games Store at the highest stable settings with owned DLC installed; use PS5 or Xbox Series X/S as strong console alternatives.

entries.remaster_caveats: Base game includes 40 licensed trucks; additional trucks are DLC and should be installed if preserving all official content.
